name: RelateAnything
description: RelateAnything: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Relation Prediction From Any Inputs
readme_summary: RelateAnything is a Python library for real-time, open-vocabulary relation prediction from any input. It allows users to define custom relation predicates at inference time without retraining, and it does not require object class labels, making it highly flexible. The model can output ranked lists of relations, or both spatial and semantic graphs simultaneously.
key_features: Predicate vocabulary supplied at inference (no retraining needed)
Object class labels are not required
Outputs ranked relation lists or spatial/semantic graphs
Runs as a single ONNX graph on CPU or in the browser
primary_use_case: Predicting relationships between objects in images or video frames using flexible, user-defined vocabularies and without relying on predefined object class labels.
cover_image_prompt: A highly detailed, 3D isometric illustration of a digital loom. Instead of threads, the loom weaves glowing lines of light that represent relationships between abstract shapes (representing objects). The user, a figure with a tablet, is actively selecting the types of 'weaves' (relations like 'above', 'next to', 'interacting with') from a floating, minimalist UI panel. The background is a clean, futuristic workshop. Subtle code snippets and data visualizations are projected onto the workbench. The overall mood is innovative and precise, with a cool, digital color palette.

name: openGym
description: Self-hosted gym & body-weight tracker — plan routines, log workouts (supersets, warm-ups, cardio), see which muscles are trained, fatigued or detrained, import from FitNotes/Strong/Hevy, passkey login. Your data, your server.
readme_summary: openGym is a self-hosted, progressive web application for tracking gym workouts and body weight. It allows users to plan routines, log sets, supersets, warm-ups, and cardio, while also visualizing muscle fatigue and training progress. The application emphasizes data ownership and privacy, offering features like passkey login and import capabilities from other fitness apps.
key_features: Muscle training, fatigue, and detraining visualization
primary_use_case: To provide users with a private, self-hosted fitness tracking solution that gives them full control over their workout data and progress.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, personal gym locker room where the lockers are made of digital blocks and glowing data streams. A user is seen interacting with a holographic interface projected from a small, personal device, which displays intricate charts of muscle engagement and workout progress. One locker door is open, revealing not gym equipment, but a clean, organized digital vault labeled 'My Data'. Subtle passkey icons float near the interface, and the overall mood is one of secure, personal control over fitness information. The art style should be a clean, modern 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear iconography and a balanced color palette.

name: Thingport
description: Collect, organize, preview, and manage your 3D printing models from the places where you discover them.
readme_summary: Thingport is a self-hosted web application designed to help 3D printing enthusiasts collect, organize, preview, and manage their 3D models from various online platforms. It provides a centralized library to prevent collections from becoming disorganized.
primary_use_case: Centralizing and managing a personal collection of 3D models from multiple online sources.
cover_image_prompt: A digital librarian meticulously organizing a vast, glowing library filled with 3D models represented as intricate, floating sculptures. The librarian, with a subtle 'Thingport' logo on their apron, uses a holographic interface to drag and drop models from various online platform icons (like stylized Thingiverse, Printables logos) into organized shelves. Each model sculpture has a small, interactive preview window displaying its 3D form. The scene is set in a clean, modern, and slightly futuristic digital space with soft, ambient lighting, emphasizing order and accessibility. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a vibrant, yet organized color palette, showcasing the seamless collection and management of digital assets.

name: maxun
description: Turn any website into a structured API. Extract, automate, search and monitor the web.
readme_summary: Maxun is an open-source web data platform designed for real-time web scraping, crawling, search, monitoring, and AI-driven data extraction. It allows users to transform any website into a structured API, enabling automation and efficient data retrieval.
primary_use_case: To enable users to extract, automate, search, and monitor data from any website by converting it into a structured API.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan, representing Maxun, stands at a workbench. In front of them is a tangled mess of raw, unorganized web pages (visualized as chaotic scrolls and scattered papers). With precise tools and glowing digital threads, the artisan is meticulously weaving these chaotic elements into a perfectly structured, organized API blueprint (visualized as a clean, glowing blueprint or a neat stack of organized data blocks). Small screens around the workbench show snippets of code and data flowing smoothly. The scene is set in a bright, modern workshop with a clean aesthetic. The overall style should be a 3D isometric illustration, emphasizing clarity and transformation, with a color palette of blues, whites, and subtle golden glows to highlight the structured output.

name: telegram-mcp
description: Telegram MCP server powered by Telethon to let MCP clients read chats, manage groups, and send/modify messages, media, contacts, and settings.
readme_summary: Telegram MCP Server is a Python-based server that bridges Telegram with Model Context Protocol (MCP) compatible clients like Claude and Cursor. It allows these clients to interact with Telegram features such as reading chats, managing groups, sending and modifying messages, and handling media and contacts.
key_features: Exposes Telegram account, chat, message, contact, media, folder, and admin operations via MCP
Supports sending, scheduling, editing, deleting, forwarding, pinning, and searching messages
Enables group and channel management, including user invites, bans, and admin roles
Facilitates contact management: listing, searching, adding, deleting, blocking, and aliasing
Offers advanced message formatting with classic and rich modes (Markdown, HTML, tables, formulas)
Includes multi-account setup, device identity management, proxy support, and chat access privacy controls
Provides Docker support for easy deployment
primary_use_case: To enable AI assistants and other MCP-compatible clients to interact with and manage Telegram accounts, chats, and messages through a standardized protocol.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, anthropomorphic robot assistant holding a glowing tablet displaying a Telegram chat interface. The robot is actively organizing and sending messages, represented by streams of digital light flowing from the tablet into a stylized, abstract representation of the Telegram network. Small, subtle UI elements showing chat management icons and contact lists are visible on the tablet screen. The background is a clean, modern digital space with soft, ambient lighting. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clarity and a slightly futuristic, approachable aesthetic. The repository name 'Telegram MCP Server' is subtly integrated into a small digital display on the robot's arm.
